target_customer: Real estate brokers and agencies in Mexico (and through them landlords and tenants) closing residential rentals
problem: Mexican tenants need a guarantor who owns property or an expensive legal policy, which slows and kills rental deals for brokers and landlords.
business_model: Fee of about 6 percent of annual lease value split between landlord and tenant, plus optional legal and home insurance
product_category: Proptech and insurtech rent guarantee, tenant screening and rental platform

founders.name: Santiago Morales
founders.background_notes: Moved to Mexico in early 2020 to help Loft expand there (TechCrunch 2024).

founders.name: Ines Gamboa Sorensen
founders.background_notes: YC page: past few years at fintech and proptech startups in Brazil.

founders.name: Diego Llano
founders.background_notes: Called CFO and cofounder by Bloomberg Linea (2021); TechCrunch caption spells the name Dylan.

competitors.name: Truehome
competitors.what: Mexican proptech named as a competitor

competitors.name: Loft
competitors.what: Brazilian proptech marketplace whose founders' employer was the source of the team

technical_complexity.rationale: Tenant screening, contract and insurance flows are standard software; the hard part is underwriting risk and collections, not engineering.

defensibility.rationale: Broker relationships (over 4,500 brokers by 2024) and underwriting data on Mexican tenants build up with volume, but guarantee products were already sold.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Well-funded marketplaces existed, but the company grew to about 1,000 leases a month by late 2024 per TechCrunch and no incumbent bought or copied it per sources found.

market_need_then: In Mexico a tenant typically needs a property-owning guarantor or a paid legal policy, a documented pain; the team saw it while building at Loft.

identity.voice_and_tone: practical, speed promise of renting in 24 hours (Expansion, 2021)

rebrands.why: Spacing change only in later press; no reason given

brand_strength.rationale: Known mainly to brokers and in startup press; no sources on brand assets or community.

outcome_analysis: Morada Uno started in October 2020 after the Loft Mexico expansion was canceled, raised a 2 million dollar seed in September 2021 and a 5.6 million dollar Series A in November 2024. By then it had worked with more than 4,500 brokers and closed over 20,000 rentals, which suggests real broker demand. It is still active and expanding to more cities, but growth numbers are company statements.
notes: Company website returned HTTP 503 on fetch. Seed figure comes from Bloomberg Linea (Spanish article); aggregators show 2.1 to 2.3M. Aggregators put total funding at 7.73M or 10M. Aptuno and Houm are named in the 2024 TechCrunch piece; only Houm also appears in the 2021 source. Name origin not stated in any source. No layoffs, shutdown or acquisition found.
